In a recent Skender podcast, during the episode labeled “Global Tech Innovation on the Fringes,” host Marissa Mateo asked Skender Founder and CEO Grant Gregson some pointed questions about digital transformation in financial services.
Gregson began the chat with an explanation of digital disruption — and contrary to the tech three-letter abbreviations we come to associate with digital — what digital disruption really means is, and what it has always meant, is disruption versus transformation.”
Two examples of digital disruptors are? Classic technology companies Airbnb and Uber have offered significantly superior user experiences compared to traditional hotel brands and taxi services. What about the relatively new financial technology firms, known as fintechs?
All these examples reside at the digital disruption end of the digital transformation spectrum, possibly even on the digital disruption spectrum itself.
Gregson, referencing the World Economic Forum’s “2017 Global Agenda Council on the Future of Financial and Monetary Systems,” calls them “super publishers,” which is, yes, yet another abbreviation of digital.
These disruptors are not the only ones adopting a more digital-first approach to customer experience or business strategy.
